description: General vendor invoice and municipal bill extraction for vendor and city-issued billing documents.

vendor_name_extract.description: Name of the company, supplier, contractor, tradesperson, service provider, utility, or vendor issuing the invoice and requesting payment, exactly as clearly printed on the document. Read it from clearly printed text — for example the remittance or payment return slip, the 'remit to' or 'make cheque payable to' line, the footer legal name or a 'does business as' clause, the vendor contact block, or a website domain — rather than a stylized logo or graphic wordmark. When the name appears both as a stylized logo and as printed body text, use the printed text. Return the printed vendor name verbatim; do not paraphrase, shorten, or invent. Do not return the customer, Invoice To party, Bill To party, property manager, property owner, tenant, attention line, technician, or contact person.

vendor_name_generate.description: Common name of the company, supplier, contractor, tradesperson, service provider, utility, or vendor issuing the invoice and requesting payment. Read the vendor name from clearly printed text — for example the remittance or payment return slip, the 'remit to' or 'make cheque payable to' line, the footer legal name or a 'does business as' clause, the vendor contact block, or a website domain — rather than a stylized logo or graphic wordmark. When the name appears both as a stylized logo and as printed body text, use the printed text. Return the short common name the vendor is known by (for example 'FortisBC', 'BC Hydro'), not the full legal-entity suffix such as 'Energy Inc.', 'Inc.', or 'Ltd'. Do not return the customer, Invoice To party, Bill To party, property manager, property owner, tenant, attention line, technician, or contact person.

invoice_date_extract.description: Date the invoice was issued. May be labeled Invoice Date, Date, Billing Date, Issue Date, Tax Invoice Date, Statement Date, or Notice Date. Return the issue date, not the due date, service date, or delivery date.

invoice_date_generate.description:
Determine the date this invoice or bill was issued. Reason step by step over the entire document:
1. Look for a date labeled Invoice Date, Date, Billing Date, Bill Date, Issue Date, Date Issued, Tax Invoice Date, Statement Date, or Notice Date. It is usually in the invoice header or the top-right invoice table, often printed next to the invoice number.
2. Never answer with the due date (Due Date, Payment Due, Payable By, Balance Due Date), a billing or service period date (Billing Period, Service From/To), a meter reading date, a service, delivery, work-performed or completion date, a payment or posting date, an account opening or closing date, a date inside a consumption-history chart or rate table, or a print timestamp or control code in the page margin.
3. A date printed together with a clock time in a page header, footer, or margin — for example '1/13/26 10:12AM' — records when the copy was printed, not when the document was issued. Never return it, not even when it is the only date on the page besides the due date.
4. If several dates are printed and only one is labeled as the invoice, bill, statement, or notice date, return that one. If a single unlabeled date is printed in the header block above the line items and no invoice date label appears anywhere, that date is the issue date; return it.
5. Return the date as printed on this document. Do not calculate it from the due date and payment terms, and never substitute the current date.
6. Return null if no issue date is printed anywhere on the document. A renewal notice or bill that shows only a payment due date and a page-footer print timestamp has no issue date: return null rather than the due date or the print timestamp.
Before answering, verify your date is not the due date, not a billing-period date, and not a page print timestamp.

payment_due_date.description: Date payment is due. May be labeled Due Date, Payment Due Date, Payable By, Due On, or Balance Due Date. Return only an explicitly printed calendar date. Do not infer from invoice date, terms, or amount. If none is printed, return null.

billing_period_start_date_extract.description: First day of the billing or service period covered by this bill. May be labeled Billing Period, Bill Period, Service Period, Service From, or From, or appear in a sentence such as 'Your bill for May 7, 2026 to Jun 5, 2026'. The period is usually printed as a date range; the start date is the first (earlier) date of the range. When the year is printed only once at the end of the range, it applies to both dates: in 'Billing period: May 19 - May 31, 2026' the start date is May 19, 2026 and counts as fully printed. Return only a start date whose day, month, and year are all printed, taking the year from the range as above when needed. Do not return the billing date, statement date, issue date, notice date, due date, payment date, meter reading date, previous reading date, an account opening or closing date, or the second (later) date of the range. If the billing period is printed only as months without day numbers (for example 'Mar/Apr 2026'), or no billing period is printed, return null.

billing_period_start_date_generate.description:
Determine the first day of the billing or service period this bill covers. Reason step by step over the entire document:
1. Look for an explicitly printed period: a 'Billing Period ... To ...' block, a 'Service From/To' line, or a sentence such as 'Your bill for May 7, 2026 to Jun 5, 2026'. The period is usually a date range and the start is the FIRST (earlier) date of the range. When the year is printed only once at the end of the range — 'Billing period: May 19 - May 31, 2026' — the year applies to both dates: the start is May 19, 2026, a fully printed date; return it.
2. Never return the second (later) date of the range, the period end date, the billing date, statement date, issue date, notice date, due date, payment date, a meter reading date, or an account opening or closing date as the start. On a final bill, 'This account was closed on <date>' names the period end, never the start.
3. If the billing period is printed only as months without day numbers (for example 'Mar/Apr 2026' or 'January-March'), return null. Do not convert months into a date.
4. Ignore consumption-history charts, rate tables, and generic billing-schedule tables (often on the back page); they do not state this bill's period.
5. Before answering, check your answer against the period end date if one is printed: the start must be strictly earlier than the end. If your candidate equals the end date, you have collapsed the range — go back to the printed range and return its first date.
6. If no billing period start date is printed anywhere on the document, return null. Do not calculate or estimate the start date from other dates or day counts.

billing_period_end_date_extract.description: Last day of the billing or service period covered by this bill. May be labeled Billing Period ... To, Service To, or To, or appear in a sentence such as 'Your bill for May 7, 2026 to Jun 5, 2026' — the end date is the second (later) date of the range. When the year is printed only once at the end of the range, it applies to both dates: in 'Billing period: May 19 - May 31, 2026' the end date is May 31, 2026. On some bills the period end coincides with the billing date or with an account closing date; return that date only when it is also printed as the end of the billing period range. Do not return the billing date, statement date, issue date, due date, payment date, or meter reading date on its own. If the billing period is printed only as months without day numbers (for example 'Mar/Apr 2026'), or no billing period range is printed, return null.

billing_period_end_date_generate.description:
Determine the last day of the billing or service period this bill covers. Reason step by step over the entire document:
1. Look for an explicitly printed period: a 'Billing Period ... To ...' block, a 'Service From/To' line, or a sentence such as 'Your bill for May 7, 2026 to Jun 5, 2026'. The end is the SECOND (later) date of the range. When the year is printed only once at the end of the range — 'Billing period: May 19 - May 31, 2026' — the year applies to both dates and the end is May 31, 2026; return it. The end date may equal the billing date or an account closing date when the printed range itself says so; on a final bill, 'This account was closed on <date>' typically matches the period end.
2. If no billing period with full dates is printed — the period is missing or shows only months (for example 'Mar/Apr 2026') — return the current meter reading date from the meter table (labeled Reading Date, or the date column next to the meter number): the date the meter was read for this bill, not the previous reading date.
3. Never return the due date or payment date, and never take dates from consumption-history charts or generic billing-schedule tables.
4. Never return the billing date unless it is explicitly printed as the end of the billing period range.
Return null only if neither a billing period with full dates nor a meter reading date is printed.

number_of_days_extract.description: Number of days in the billing or metering period, as printed on the bill. It may appear: in the meter reading table under a column labeled DAYS, NO. OF DAYS, or Number of Days; in a basic or daily charge line such as 'Basic Charge 30 days x $0.2999/day' or 'Basic charge (13 days at 0.4216 per day)'; or in text such as '3,420 kWh used over 30 days'. A value in a DAYS column or multiplying a per-day rate in a basic charge line is definitive — return that day count exactly as printed. Return the day count only. Do not return the meter reading Difference, a meter reading, consumption, kWh, cubic meters, GJ, a per-day or per-GJ rate (such as 0.4216 or 8.469), a multiplier, or a dollar amount. Return null if no day count is printed.

number_of_days_generate.description:
Determine the number of days in the billing or metering period for this bill. Reason step by step:
1. Look in the meter reading table for a column labeled DAYS, NO. OF DAYS, or Number of Days; that value is definitive — return it.
2. Otherwise look for a basic or daily charge line where a day count multiplies a per-day rate — 'Basic Charge 30 days x $0.2999/day' or 'Basic charge (13 days at 0.4216 per day)' — or text such as '3,420 kWh used over 30 days', and return the day count.
3. The value is a count of days: usually 25 to 130, but a final or opening bill can legitimately cover fewer days (the printed count is correct even when small). Never return a meter reading, the reading Difference, consumption, kWh, cubic meters, GJ, a per-day or per-GJ rate (such as 0.4216), a multiplier, or a dollar amount.
4. Do not calculate the number of days from the billing period dates; return only a printed value.
5. Return null if no day count is printed anywhere.

invoice_number_extract.description: Unique invoice identifier assigned by the vendor for this invoice. Prefer the value in the invoice header or top-right invoice table that is directly labeled Invoice #, Invoice No., Invoice Number, Inv #, Inv No., Tax Invoice No., Bill Number, Document Number, License Number, License No., License #, Licence Number, Licence No., or Licence #. The invoice number is often near the invoice date. On a business licence or permit renewal bill, 'Licence #' is usually a column header in the licence fee table in the middle of the page (columns such as Licence #, Licence Type, Locations, and fee amounts) and again on the tear-off payment stub at the bottom; on such a bill the invoice number is the value in the table cell directly below the Licence # column header — a short identifier, for example two digits, a dash, and a serial number — not a value from the top-right header area. On such a bill do not return the value labeled Account number (that is the customer's account number, not the invoice number), and do not return a digit string printed under or beside a barcode. If the document includes both an invoice page and a work order page, prefer the value labeled Invoice # on the invoice page; use a standalone '#:' value on the work order page only if it matches the invoice page number. Return only the identifier value, not the label. Do not return P.O. No., PO #, PO number, job number, work order number, project number, reference number, customer number, account number, vendor GST number, tax ID, phone number, postal code, product registration number, date, subtotal, GST amount, total amount, balance due, service address, a payment return slip number or remittance slip reference number, or a document control number or unlabeled print-control code printed in the page margin (often rotated and 'P'-prefixed, for example 'P000017576-C000036395-12-VIP'). Water, sewer, and metered-utility bills, and natural gas bills such as FortisBC, carry only a customer account number and have NO vendor-assigned invoice number: on these bills return null. In particular, a short unlabeled number printed on or immediately after the bill's title or heading — for example the 1243 in 'UTILITY NOTICE 1243', the 11802 in 'UTILITY BILL 11802', or a number such as 1740 or 12339 following a 'Metered Utility Bill' heading — is a notice or form number, NOT an invoice number; never return it. A BC Hydro electricity bill, by contrast, does print a real invoice number, so extract it, and a city business licence or permit renewal notice carries a licence number, which is handled above. When a bill has no value clearly labeled as an invoice, bill, or document number, return null rather than the account number, a number beside the title, a payment slip or remittance reference number, or a margin control code.

invoice_number_generate.description:
Determine the unique invoice identifier the vendor assigned to this invoice. Reason step by step over the entire document:
1. First check whether this is a business licence or permit renewal bill (a city-issued notice with a licence fee table and a licence type or category). If it is, the licence number is the invoice number. It is labeled License Number, License No., License #, Licence Number, Licence No., or Licence # — and on these bills that label is usually a column header in the licence fee table in the middle of the page (columns such as Licence #, Licence Type, Locations, and fee amounts) and again on the tear-off payment stub at the bottom, so read the value from the table cell directly below the Licence # column header. It is a short identifier, for example two digits, a dash, and a serial number; the exact format varies by municipality. On these bills never answer with the value labeled Account number in the top-right header area — that is the customer's account number, not the invoice number — and never answer with a digit string printed under or beside a barcode.
2. Otherwise, prefer the value in the invoice header or top-right invoice table directly labeled Invoice #, Invoice No., Invoice Number, Inv #, Inv No., Tax Invoice No., Bill Number, or Document Number. It is often printed near the invoice date.
3. If the document includes both an invoice page and a work order page, prefer the value labeled Invoice # on the invoice page; use a standalone '#:' value on the work order page only if it matches the invoice page number.
4. Never answer with a P.O. No., PO number, job number, work order number, project number, reference number, customer number, account number, vendor GST number, tax ID, phone number, postal code, product registration number, a payment return slip or remittance slip reference number, a document control number or unlabeled print-control code printed in the page margin (often rotated and 'P'-prefixed, for example 'P000017576-C000036395-12-VIP'), a date, a subtotal, GST amount, total amount, balance due, or a service address. If a candidate matches one of these, discard it and keep looking — on a licence bill the correct value is in the licence fee table.
5. Recognise a utility account statement that carries no vendor-assigned invoice number. Water, sewer, and metered-utility bills, and natural gas bills such as FortisBC, have only a customer account number and NO invoice number: return an empty string for these. Watch for the trap — these bills often print a short unlabeled number on or immediately after their title or heading ('UTILITY NOTICE 1243', 'UTILITY BILL 11802', a 'Metered Utility Bill' heading followed by 1740 or 12339). That is a notice or form number, not an invoice number; never answer with it, and do not treat it as a reason to stop returning an empty string. A BC Hydro electricity bill, by contrast, does print a real invoice number, so return it; a city business licence or permit renewal notice carries a licence number, handled in step 1.
6. Return only the identifier value, not the label.
Before answering, verify the value identifies THIS invoice and is not the customer's account number, a barcode digit string, a payment slip or margin control code, or a PO/job number. Return an empty string only if no invoice identifier appears anywhere on the document.

po_or_job_number_extract.description: Purchase order, job, work order, contract, project, or reference number. It is exactly 8 digits and always starts with 11 or 33 (for example 11024580 or 33001022). The digits may be printed with spaces between them (for example '1102 4580'); remove the spaces and return the 8 digits only, with no letters, dashes, or other punctuation. The number may also be printed inside parentheses or square brackets (for example '(11024580)' or '[33001022]'); ignore the surrounding brackets and return only the 8 digits. May be labeled PO #, P.O. No., Purchase Order, Customer PO, Job #, Job No., Job Number, Work Order, WO, Contract #, Contract No., Contract Number, Project No., Site Ref, Customer Ref, or Reference — or may appear unlabeled or after a bare '#'. Ignore candidates containing letters, and ignore values with 9 or more digits even when they carry a PO label — look elsewhere on the document for the 8-digit number starting with 11 or 33. If both a PO and a Job number exist, return the PO number. Return null if no 8-digit value starting with 11 or 33 is present.

po_or_job_number_generate.description:
Determine the buyer's purchase order or job number for this invoice. Reason step by step over the entire document:
1. The number is exactly 8 digits and always starts with 11 or 33 (examples: 11024580, 33001022). This format rule is absolute: a value that does not match it is never the answer, no matter how it is labeled.
2. Scan the whole document — header, bill-to / sold-to / customer block, subject and reference lines, contract lines, line-item descriptions, and footer — and collect every digit sequence that could match. Digits may be printed with spaces between them (for example '1102 4580' means 11024580); remove spaces before testing the format. The number may also appear inside parentheses or square brackets (for example '(11024580)' or '[33001022]'); strip the brackets before testing the format.
3. Candidates may be labeled PO #, P.O. No., Purchase Order, Customer PO, Job #, Job No., Job Number, Work Order, WO, Contract #, Contract No., Contract Number, Project No., Site Ref, Customer Ref, or Reference — but the number often appears unlabeled, after a bare '#', or immediately next to the customer name (for example 'NOBLE & ASSOCIATES PROPERTY MANAGEMENT # 11022266' means the number is 11022266).
4. If a labeled value fails the rule in step 1 (for example a 9-digit value on a 'Customer PO No.' line), discard it and keep looking — the correct 8-digit 11/33 number is usually printed elsewhere on the document, such as a Contract # or Job # line.
5. Never answer with a GST registration number, phone number, fax number, invoice number, account number, customer number, quote number, or any part of an address or date.
6. If multiple distinct matching numbers exist, prefer the one labeled PO; if the same number repeats, return it once.
Return only the 8 digits, with no spaces or punctuation. Before answering, verify your answer is exactly 8 digits and starts with 11 or 33. Return an empty string only if, after scanning the entire document, no 8-digit number starting with 11 or 33 appears anywhere.

gst_amount_extract.description: Canadian GST (5%) amount charged on the whole bill. Prefer the amount directly labeled GST, G.S.T., GST@5.0%, GST 5%, or Goods and Services Tax. Return the numeric amount charged, not the rate and not the base amount the GST was calculated on: 'GST 5% on $63.22 ... $3.17' means 3.17. Some bills — utility bills in particular — split their charges into sections and print a separate GST line under each section, for example 'TAXES ON ACCOUNT CHARGES * GST 5% $0.68' and 'TAXES ON ELECTRICITY CHARGES * GST 5% on $49.72 $2.49'. On such a bill each section line is only part of the tax: the bill's total GST is printed in the tax recap near the end of the bill details — a TAX SUMMARY, Sales Tax Summary, Total GST, or Total Taxes block stating the GST charged on the bill's full pre-tax amount, for example 'TAX SUMMARY GST 5% on $63.22 ... $3.17'. When a GST amount is printed under more than one section, return that bill-level GST amount and never a single section's GST line; if no bill-level GST amount is printed on such a bill, return null rather than one section's amount. When GST is charged in only one place, that single amount is the answer. Some vendors label the tax row generically instead of naming GST. When no row anywhere is labeled GST, and the totals block shows a single tax row labeled only Tax, Taxes, Sales Tax, or Tax amount, that row is the GST provided its amount is about 5% of the subtotal — for example 'sub Total $796.00 / Tax $39.80 / Total $835.80' means 39.80, and a printed GST registration number such as 'GST# 122990112RT' elsewhere on the page confirms the vendor charges GST. Return that amount (never the registration number itself). If the single generically labeled tax amount is materially more than 5% of the subtotal — about 12%, which combines GST and PST — it is a combined tax: return null. On handwritten and receipt-book invoices the amount column is often split into dollars and cents sub-columns separated by a printed vertical rule, with no decimal point: a GST row showing 4 in the dollars sub-column and 50 in the cents sub-column means 4.50. Read both sub-columns and return the full decimal amount including the cents; never return the dollars sub-column alone. If a separate provincial sales tax (PST) line is present, return only the GST line, not PST and not a combined Total Tax; a tax summary or recap that itemises GST on its own line is a GST line, not a combined Total Tax. Use a combined Total Tax only when there is no separate GST line anywhere and no other tax types are present. Do not return the GST registration number, subtotal, total, or balance due.

gst_amount_generate.description:
Determine the Canadian GST (5%) amount charged on this invoice. Reason step by step:
1. Collect every amount labeled GST, G.S.T., GST@5.0%, GST 5%, or Goods and Services Tax. Read the amount charged, not the rate and not the base amount the GST was calculated on: 'GST 5% on $63.22 ... $3.17' means 3.17.
2. If GST is charged in only one place, that amount is the answer.
3. If no row anywhere is labeled GST, check the totals block for a single tax row labeled only Tax, Taxes, Sales Tax, or Tax amount. When the vendor prints a GST registration number somewhere on the page (for example 'GST# 122990112RT') and charges that one tax, and its amount is about 5% of the subtotal, that row IS the GST: return it — 'sub Total $796.00 / Tax $39.80 / Total $835.80' means 39.80. Never answer with the registration number itself. If that single tax amount is materially more than 5% of the subtotal (about 12% combines GST and PST), it is a combined tax: return an empty value.
4. If more than one GST amount is printed, the bill splits its charges into sections and taxes each section separately — for example 'TAXES ON ACCOUNT CHARGES * GST 5% $0.68' and 'TAXES ON ELECTRICITY CHARGES * GST 5% on $49.72 $2.49'. The answer is the GST for the WHOLE bill, never one section's line: take the amount from the tax recap printed near the end of the bill details — a TAX SUMMARY, Sales Tax Summary, Total GST, or Total Taxes block stating the GST on the bill's full pre-tax amount, for example 'TAX SUMMARY GST 5% on $63.22 ... $3.17' means 3.17. If no such recap is printed, add the section GST amounts together (0.68 + 2.49 = 3.17).
5. On handwritten and receipt-book invoices the amount column is often split into dollars and cents sub-columns separated by a printed vertical rule, with no decimal point: a GST row showing 4 in the dollars sub-column and 50 in the cents sub-column means 4.50. Combine both sub-columns and return the full decimal amount including the cents; never drop the cents.
6. Verify the amount: GST is normally about 5% of the bill's pre-tax amount (the total minus the GST). If your answer is much smaller than that, you have most likely returned one section's GST instead of the bill's total — go back to step 4. If your read is off by less than one dollar, re-check for a missed cents sub-column.
7. If a separate provincial sales tax (PST) line is present, return only the GST, not PST and not a combined Total Tax; a tax summary or recap that itemises GST on its own line is a GST line, not a combined Total Tax. Use a combined Total Tax only when no separate GST line appears anywhere and no other tax types are present.
8. Never answer with the GST registration number, the subtotal, the total, or the balance due.
Return an empty value if no GST is charged.

pst_amount_extract.description: British Columbia PST (Provincial Sales Tax, 7%) amount charged. Prefer the amount directly labeled PST, P.S.T., PST (BC), PST BC, PST@7%, PST @ 7%, PST 7%, or Provincial Sales Tax. Return the numeric dollar amount, not the rate. Most invoices are for services and charge no PST: if no PST line is printed, return null. If a PST line is printed but its value is N/A, n/a, nil, a dash, or blank, no PST was charged — return null. In the totals area the PST amount box often sits directly beside the GST amount box; read the value from the PST box only, never the GST box, even when the GST amount is larger. On handwritten and receipt-book invoices the amount column is often split into dollars and cents sub-columns separated by a printed vertical rule, with no decimal point: a PST row showing 4 in the dollars sub-column and 50 in the cents sub-column means 4.50. Read both sub-columns and return the full decimal amount including the cents; never return the dollars sub-column alone. Return only the PST line amount, never the GST line and never a combined Total Tax. Do not return the vendor's PST registration number from the document header or footer (labeled PST#, PST No., or PST Number, for example 'PST#: 1012-5388'), the GST amount, a GST/PST tax-code entry in a line-item TAX column, the subtotal, total, or balance due.

pst_amount_generate.description:
Determine the British Columbia PST (Provincial Sales Tax, 7%) amount charged on this invoice. Reason step by step:
1. Look for a PST line or box in the totals area — labeled PST, P.S.T., PST (BC), PST BC, PST@7%, PST 7%, or Provincial Sales Tax. The PST box often sits directly beside the GST box; read the PST value, never the GST value, even when the GST amount is larger.
2. Most invoices are for services and charge no PST. If no PST line or box appears anywhere on the document, return an empty value.
3. If a PST line is printed but its value is N/A, n/a, nil, a dash, or blank, PST was considered and not charged: the answer is 0.
4. On handwritten and receipt-book invoices the amount column is often split into dollars and cents sub-columns separated by a printed vertical rule, with no decimal point: a PST row showing 4 in the dollars sub-column and 50 in the cents sub-column means 4.50. Combine both sub-columns; never drop the cents.
5. Verify the amount: BC PST is 7%, but it is often charged on only the goods, parts, or materials portion of the invoice — labour and services are usually PST-exempt. The PST amount should be about 7% of either the full pre-tax amount or the parts/materials subtotal (for example, PST of 34.75 on an invoice with a Parts Total of 496.41 and a Labor Total of 439.00 is correct: 7% of the parts only). Never reject or recompute a printed PST amount merely because it is not 7% of the whole subtotal; if your read is off by less than one dollar, re-check for a missed cents sub-column.
6. Never answer with the GST amount, a combined Total Tax, the vendor's PST registration number (labeled PST#, PST No., or PST Number, for example '1012-5388'), a GST/PST tax-code entry in a line-item TAX column, the subtotal, total, or balance due. A line labeled 'BC GST' is GST, not PST — the 'BC' prefix does not make it PST.
Return the numeric PST dollar amount: 0 when a printed PST line shows N/A or no amount; an empty value when no PST line exists.

total_invoice_amount_extract.description: Amount the recipient must pay for THIS bill's own charges, including all of this bill's taxes. It never includes a balance carried over from earlier bills — treat any prior amount as already paid. Start by reading how much is carried forward: the Balance Forward, Previous Balance, Previous Amount Due, or aged-arrears amount. Use the amount actually carried forward, not a Previous bill line that has since been settled — a bill printing 'Previous bill $627.90' together with 'BALANCE FORWARD $0.00' carries nothing forward. When a NON-ZERO amount is carried forward, do NOT return the Total Due, Total Amount Due, Balance Due, or Total Account Balance Due that contains it, however prominently it is printed; return this bill's own charges instead — the figure labeled Current Charges, Current Invoice Charges, Total Current Charges, or New Charges when one is printed, otherwise the bill's own tax-inclusive charges subtotal, which equals the Total Due minus the amount carried forward. Examples: 'Previous Balance 1,352.93 / Current Invoice Charges 1,626.20 / Total Account Balance Due 2,979.13' means 1626.20; 'BALANCE FORWARD $24.32 / ELECTRICITY CHARGES SUBTOTAL $11.37 / TOTAL DUE $35.69' means 11.37. When nothing is carried forward — no such line is printed, or it shows 0.00 — take the value labeled Total, Invoice Total, Amount Due, Balance Due, Total Due, Grand Total, Amount Payable, or Please Pay (if Total and Balance Due are both present and equal, return that amount), even when a smaller Current charges figure is printed elsewhere on the page. The difference is then a charge billed on THIS bill that the vendor's Current charges box leaves out, such as a security deposit, account set-up charge, or connection fee itemised among the bill's own charges and payable on its due date. Example: 'Security deposit $177.00 / Current charges $21.14 / Total due $198.14' with 'BALANCE FORWARD $0.00' means 198.14. On handwritten and receipt-book invoices the amount column is often split into dollars and cents sub-columns separated by a printed vertical rule, with no decimal point: a total row showing 94 in the dollars sub-column and 50 in the cents sub-column means 94.50. Read both sub-columns and return the full decimal amount including the cents; never return the dollars sub-column alone. PROPERTY TAX NOTICES FOLLOW TWO EXTRA RULES THAT OVERRIDE THE GENERAL ONES ABOVE. (a) GRANT COLUMNS: a BC property tax notice prints its totals three times, once per home owner grant column — a no-grant column headed 'No Grant', 'A - NO GRANT', 'COLUMN A NO GRANT', 'A. NO GRANT' or 'No Grant A', then a basic or regular grant column, then an additional or senior grant column. Always return the NO-GRANT figure, which is the largest of the three, read from the notice's own total row (Total Outstanding Taxes, Total Amount Due, Amount Due, Net Amount Due, Total Taxes Due, Total Current Taxes, or Balance). Take it only from that total row: a 'No Grant' amount quoted in a sentence about next year's estimated monthly instalments or a pre-authorised payment plan is not this bill's total. (b) ARREARS: on a property tax notice, unpaid arrears, delinquent taxes and their interest from prior years are still payable and ARE part of the amount due, so include them and return the arrears-inclusive total. Example: 'Total taxes and other charges 6,032.62 / Unpaid arrears taxes 125.66 / TOTAL OUTSTANDING TAXES DUE 6,158.28' means 6158.28. This reverses the carried-forward rule above, and applies ONLY to property tax notices. A prepayment, credit or adjustment line is not arrears — it reduces what is owed, and the notice's net amount due already reflects it. Do not return a pre-tax subtotal that excludes this bill's taxes, the GST amount, an amount already paid, an individual line amount, the previous balance, the balance forward, or a total-account-balance that includes a prior unpaid balance.

total_invoice_amount_generate.description:
Determine the final amount the recipient must pay for THIS bill, including all taxes and charges. Reason step by step:
1. Find the total row — labeled Total, Invoice Total, Amount Due, Balance Due, Total Due, Grand Total, Amount Payable, or Please Pay. If Total and Balance Due are both present and equal, that is the amount.
2. Find how much is carried over from earlier bills: read the Balance Forward, Previous Balance, Previous Amount Due, or aged-arrears line. Treat any such prior amount as already paid — it is never part of this bill's own charges. Use the amount actually carried forward, not a Previous bill line that has since been settled: 'Previous bill $627.90' printed together with 'BALANCE FORWARD $0.00' carries nothing forward.
3. If nothing is carried forward (no such line, or it shows 0.00), the Total / Total Due / Balance Due IS this bill's amount. Return it even when a smaller Current charges figure is printed elsewhere on the page: the difference between them is then a charge billed on THIS bill that the Current charges box leaves out, such as a security deposit, account set-up charge, or connection fee itemised among the bill's own charges and payable on its due date. Example: 'Security deposit $177.00 / Current charges $21.14 / Total due $198.14' with 'BALANCE FORWARD $0.00' means 198.14.
4. If a NON-ZERO amount is carried forward and the Total Due adds it to this bill's charges, the answer is this bill's own charges (they already include this bill's taxes): the figure labeled Current Charges, Current Invoice Charges, Total Current Charges, or New Charges when one is printed, otherwise the bill's own charges subtotal, which equals the Total Due minus the amount carried forward. Check the arithmetic: carried-forward amount + this bill's charges, adjusted by any payments or adjustments shown, should equal the Total Due. Examples: 'BALANCE FORWARD $24.32 / ELECTRICITY CHARGES SUBTOTAL $11.37 / TOTAL DUE $35.69' means 11.37; 'Previous Balance 1,352.93 / Current Invoice Charges 1,626.20 / Total Account Balance Due 2,979.13' means 1626.20.
5. Property tax notices override steps 1-4 in two ways. First, they print their totals three times, once per home owner grant column: a no-grant column headed 'No Grant', 'A - NO GRANT', 'COLUMN A NO GRANT', 'A. NO GRANT' or 'No Grant A', then a basic or regular grant column, then an additional or senior grant column. Return the NO-GRANT figure — the largest of the three — from the notice's own total row (Total Outstanding Taxes, Total Amount Due, Amount Due, Net Amount Due, Total Taxes Due, Total Current Taxes, Balance), never from a sentence about next year's estimated instalments or a pre-authorised payment plan. Second, unpaid arrears, delinquent taxes and their interest from prior years remain payable on a property tax notice and ARE part of the amount due: include them and return the arrears-inclusive total — 'Total taxes and other charges 6,032.62 / Unpaid arrears taxes 125.66 / TOTAL OUTSTANDING TAXES DUE 6,158.28' means 6158.28. This reverses step 4 for property tax notices only. A prepayment, credit or adjustment line is not arrears: it reduces what is owed and the net amount due already reflects it.
6. Check how the amount is written. On handwritten and receipt-book invoices the amount column is often split into dollars and cents sub-columns separated by a printed vertical rule, with no decimal point: a total row showing 94 in the dollars sub-column and 50 in the cents sub-column means 94.50. Combine both sub-columns; never drop the cents.
7. Verify the amount. The bill's own charge sections plus the amount carried forward should add up to the printed Total Due (for example 'ACCOUNT CHARGES SUBTOTAL $191.18' plus 'ELECTRICITY CHARGES SUBTOTAL $6.96' with nothing carried forward gives $198.14). On a simple invoice with line amounts or a subtotal and a GST amount, the total should equal their sum (for example a line amount of 90 plus GST of 4.50 gives a total of 94.50). When every charge on the bill is taxable, GST is about 5% of your answer minus GST, and an answer far larger than that is a sign you have swept in an amount carried forward — go back to step 4. That check does not apply when the bill itemises a non-taxable charge such as a security deposit or other refundable amount: those carry no GST, so the answer legitimately exceeds (GST divided by 5%) plus GST, and you must not shrink it to match the GST. If your read of the total is off by less than one dollar, re-check for a missed cents sub-column.
8. Never answer with the subtotal, the GST amount, an amount already paid, an individual line amount, the previous balance, the balance forward, or a total-account-balance that includes a prior unpaid balance.
Return the full decimal amount including the cents.

service_address_extract.description: Address where the work, service, delivery, security monitoring, fire monitoring, repair, utility service, or billed property is located. Treat labels in this priority order: 1) SHIP TO / Ship To / Shipped To / Ship-to, especially when followed by text such as "the Premises", "Premises", "Site", or "Site Location"; 2) Service Address, Service Location, Site Address, Site Location, Job Address, Work Location, Prepared For, Property Address, Premises, Installation Address, or Service For; 3) for municipal bills only, the assessed or billed property address; 4) last resort, used ONLY when none of the labels in 1-3 appears anywhere on the document: an address printed under an Attention or Attn heading. On a small trade or contractor invoice the serviced property is commonly addressed that way and there is no other candidate — for example 'Attention: / 6240 Cooney Road, / Richmond, BC / Canada' means the work was done at '6240 Cooney Road, Richmond, BC', so return it rather than treating it as a mailing block to exclude. Never take the vendor's own contact block for this (the address printed alongside the vendor's phone number, email address, or logo, usually at the top of the page), and if the Attention heading is followed only by a person or department name with no street address, there is no service address under it. When a document has both SOLD TO / Customer / Bill To / Invoice To and SHIP TO / Premises / Site blocks, always return the SHIP TO / Premises / Site address, not the SOLD TO or customer mailing address. On private waste-hauler and route-service invoices the served site is printed inside the DETAILS or line-item section as a site header rather than under any of the labels above: a line that begins with a parenthesised site sequence number and site name and carries a site PO reference labelled SITEPO, SC#, or SC (for example '(0001) NOBLE<<1942 KINGSWAY>> SITEPO 33001163' or '(0001) CONNAUGHT PLAZA SC#33000152'), immediately followed by the site's street-address line, which commonly ends in a 'CSA' site code. Treat that street-address line as the service address: return only the street, city, and province, dropping the parenthesised index, the site name and any '<<...>>' fragment, the SITEPO/SC# number, and the trailing 'CSA <code>' marker; a postal code is usually not printed here, so return the address without it. Example: from '(0001) NOBLE<<1942 KINGSWAY>> SITEPO 33001163' / '1942 KINGSWAY, VANCOUVER BC CSA 1740', return '1942 KINGSWAY, VANCOUVER BC'. For The Radius Group invoices, the service address is the address directly under SHIP TO (the "Premises"). In that layout, exclude the customer/company name line and return only the street, city, province/state, and postal code if printed. Example: if the block is "SHIP TO (the Premises) / 1100289 BC LTD / 1606 Broadway W / Vancouver, BC", return "1606 Broadway W\nVancouver, BC". Do not return the vendor's own office address, remittance address, logo/header address, SOLD TO address, Invoice To address, Bill To address, customer mailing address, account owner, property manager name, or company name line. Exception: those exclusions apply only to an address whose only label is SOLD TO, Bill To, Invoice To, or an unlabeled mailing block. If an address appears under one of the priority labels above (such as Prepared For, Service Address, or Site Address), return it even when the same address also appears in a Bill To / Invoice To block or doubles as the customer mailing address; on utility and sub-metering bills the served unit is often also the mailing address. Whatever the source block, return exactly these parts and nothing else, in this order: the street line (including any unit or suite), the city, the province or state, and the postal code if one is printed. Never include a country line such as 'Canada' or 'CANADA', a customer or company name line, a care-of ('c/o') line, an attention person's name, or a property manager or account owner name — not even when they appear inside the same block as the street address. Drop the customer name line and return only the street, city, province/state, and postal code. Drop that name line even when it begins with digits repeating the street number: from 'Details for Service Location: 2993 Granville Limited Partnership, 2993 Granville St, Vancouver Bc V6h 3j6' return '2993 Granville St, Vancouver Bc V6h 3j6', never the leading partnership or company name. Example: if the block is "Prepared For: / Yang, Hong Li and Zhen Shao / #511 - 5233 Gilbert Road / Richmond, BC V7C 0B3", return "#511 - 5233 Gilbert Road\nRichmond, BC V7C 0B3".

service_address_generate.description: Determine the address where the work, service, delivery, security monitoring, fire monitoring, repair, utility service, or billed property is located, and return it as a clean address. Prioritise the SHIP TO / Ship To / Shipped To block (especially when labelled 'the Premises', 'Premises', 'Site', or 'Site Location'), then Service Address, Service Location, Site Address, Site Location, Job Address, Work Location, Property Address, Prepared For, Installation Address, or Service For; for municipal bills, the assessed or billed property address. As a last resort ONLY — when none of those labels appears anywhere on the document — use an address printed under an Attention or Attn heading: on a small trade or contractor invoice the serviced property is commonly addressed that way and nothing else on the page names it, so 'Attention: / 6240 Cooney Road, / Richmond, BC / Canada' means the work was done at '6240 Cooney Road, Richmond, BC'. Return it rather than dismissing it as a mailing block. Never use the vendor's own contact block for this (the address printed alongside the vendor's phone number, email address, or logo), and if the Attention heading carries only a person or department name with no street address, there is no service address under it. When both a SOLD TO / Customer / Bill To / Invoice To block and a SHIP TO / Premises / Site block are present, always use the SHIP TO / Premises / Site location, never the SOLD TO or customer mailing address. On private waste-hauler and route-service invoices the served site is not under any of those labels — it is printed inside the DETAILS or line-item section as a site header: a line beginning with a parenthesised site sequence number and site name and carrying a site PO reference labelled SITEPO, SC#, or SC (for example '(0001) NOBLE<<1942 KINGSWAY>> SITEPO 33001163' or '(0001) CONNAUGHT PLAZA SC#33000152'), immediately followed by the site's street-address line, which commonly ends in a 'CSA' site code. Use that street-address line as the service address: return only the street, city, and province, dropping the parenthesised index, the site name and any '<<...>>' fragment, the SITEPO/SC# number, and the trailing 'CSA <code>' marker; a postal code is usually not printed here. Example: from '(0001) NOBLE<<1942 KINGSWAY>> SITEPO 33001163' / '1942 KINGSWAY, VANCOUVER BC CSA 1740', return '1942 KINGSWAY, VANCOUVER BC'. Whatever the source block, assemble exactly these parts and nothing else, in this order: the street line (including any unit or suite), the city, the province or state, and the postal code if one is printed. Never include a country line such as 'Canada' or 'CANADA', a customer or company name line, a care-of ('c/o') line, an attention person's name, or a property manager or account owner name — not even when they appear inside the same block as the street address. Exclude the vendor's own office or remittance address and any logo or header address. Exclude that name line even when it begins with digits repeating the street number: from 'Details for Service Location: 2993 Granville Limited Partnership, 2993 Granville St, Vancouver Bc V6h 3j6' return '2993 Granville St, Vancouver Bc V6h 3j6', never the leading partnership or company name. Exception: the exclusions apply only to an address whose only label is SOLD TO, Bill To, or Invoice To, or to an unlabeled mailing block. An address under a priority label such as Prepared For or Service Address is the service address even when it is identical to the Bill To / Invoice To or mailing address, which is common on utility and sub-metering bills. Example: from "Prepared For: / Yang, Hong Li and Zhen Shao / #511 - 5233 Gilbert Road / Richmond, BC V7C 0B3", return "#511 - 5233 Gilbert Road\nRichmond, BC V7C 0B3". Return an empty string if undeterminable.

bill_to_address_extract.description: Address printed in the customer / recipient block of the invoice — the party being billed — commonly labeled BILL TO, Bill To, Billed To, SOLD TO, Sold To, Invoice To, Customer, or Client. Return only the address itself, in this order: the street line (including any unit or suite), the city, the province or state, and the postal code if one is printed. Never include the customer or company name line (for example 'Noble & Associates Property Management'), a care-of ('c/o') line, an attention person's name, any bracketed job or reference line (for example '[Job# 11024565]'), or a country line such as 'Canada' or 'CANADA' — even when they appear inside the same block as the street address. Do not return the vendor's own contact, header, remittance, or logo address (the address printed alongside the vendor's phone number, email address, or logo). Return an empty string if there is no Bill To / customer block.

bill_to_address_generate.description: Determine the address printed in the customer / recipient block of the invoice — the party being billed, commonly labeled BILL TO, Bill To, Billed To, SOLD TO, Sold To, Invoice To, Customer, or Client — and return it as a clean address. Assemble only the address parts, in this order: the street line (including any unit or suite), the city, the province or state, and the postal code if one is printed. Exclude the customer or company name line (for example 'Noble & Associates Property Management'), a care-of ('c/o') line, an attention person's name, any bracketed job or reference line (for example '[Job# 11024565]'), and any country line such as 'Canada' or 'CANADA', even when they appear inside the same block as the street address. Never use the vendor's own contact, header, remittance, or logo address (the address printed alongside the vendor's phone number, email address, or logo). Return an empty string if undeterminable.

account_number_extract.description: Customer account number assigned by the biller — the stable identifier for the customer's ongoing account with the vendor, utility, or municipality, exactly as printed on the document. May be labeled Account Number, Account No., Account #, Acct #, Acct No., Acct Number, Customer Account, Customer Account Number, Utility Account, Utility Account Number, Customer Number, Customer #, Customer No., Client Number, Client #, Client No., Folio, Folio Number, Folio No., or Roll Number. It usually appears in the account summary block near the top of the bill and again on the remittance stub or payment return slip at the bottom. Remove any spaces printed between digit or letter groups, but keep dashes, dots, and all other punctuation exactly as printed (for example '1234 5678 9012' becomes '123456789012'; '12345-001' stays '12345-001'). Letters are allowed. Do not return the invoice number, statement number, bill number, PO number, job number, work order number, GST registration number, business number, meter number, rate class, licence number, permit number, cheque number, phone or fax number, a date, or a dollar amount. Return null if no account number is printed.

account_number_generate.description:
Determine the customer's account number on this bill — the stable identifier the biller (vendor, utility, or municipality) has assigned to the customer's account. Reason step by step over the entire document:
1. The account number identifies the customer's ongoing account with the biller, so it is unchanged from bill to bill. It is usually printed in the account summary near the top of the bill and repeated on the remittance stub or payment return slip at the bottom — an identifier printed in both places is almost always the account number.
2. Scan the whole document — account summary, header, customer/service block, payment instructions, and remittance stub — and collect every candidate labeled Account Number, Account No., Account #, Acct Number, Acct #, Acct No., Customer Account, Customer Account Number, Utility Account, Utility Account Number, Customer Number, Customer #, Customer No., Client Number, Client #, Client No., Folio, Folio Number, Folio No., or Roll Number.
3. Do not confuse it with per-bill identifiers: an invoice number, statement number, or bill number changes with every bill and is never the account number. If a candidate is labeled Invoice, Statement, or Bill, discard it and keep looking.
4. Never answer with a PO number, job number, work order number, GST registration number, business number, meter number, rate class, licence number, permit number, cheque number, phone or fax number, a date, a dollar amount, or any part of an address or postal code.
5. If multiple distinct candidates remain, prefer the one printed on the remittance stub; on a property-tax bill the Folio or Roll Number is the account number.
6. Normalize the answer: remove spaces printed between digit or letter groups, but keep dashes, dots, and all other punctuation exactly as printed (for example '1234 5678 9012' means 123456789012; '12345-001' stays 12345-001).
Before answering, verify the value is the customer's account identifier and not an invoice or statement number. Return an empty string only if, after scanning the entire document, no account number appears anywhere.

folio_number_extract.description: The folio or roll number that identifies the property on a property tax notice, exactly as printed. May be labeled Folio, Folio Number, Folio No., Folio/Roll, Roll, Roll Number, Roll No., or Roll/Folio, and is often printed beside a short Jurisdiction code. It appears in the property details block near the top of the notice and again on the remittance stub at the bottom. Keep dashes, dots, letters and leading zeros exactly as printed, but remove spaces printed between digit groups (for example '631 000816.058' becomes '631000816.058'). Do not return the jurisdiction number on its own (a short three-digit municipality code such as 306 or 221), the PID or parcel identifier, the access code, the plan, lot or block number, the legal description, the customer or bulk owner code, a postal code, a date, or a dollar amount. When the notice prints BOTH a Folio and a Roll number and the two differ, return the FOLIO value: the roll number is usually the folio with a jurisdiction prefix or a trailing sub-account added (folio '328-314-00-0' against roll 'D-328-314-00-0', folio '1987-9000-7' against roll '051-1987-9000-7', folio '23-0122-012' against roll '23-0122-012-000', folio '000592.002' against roll '0000592.002'). Only when no Folio label is printed at all does the Roll number become the answer. When the notice prints a separate account number as well, return the folio or roll value and not the account number. Return null when the document is not a property tax notice, or prints no folio or roll number.

folio_number_generate.description:
Determine the folio or roll number that identifies the property on this document. Reason step by step:
1. First decide whether this is a property tax notice — a document assessing annual property taxes for a municipality or a province, usually titled Property Tax Notice, Property Tax Bill, Advance Tax Notice, or Services Levy. If it is not, return null: no other kind of document carries a folio number.
2. Scan the property details block near the top and the remittance stub at the bottom, and collect every candidate labeled Folio, Folio Number, Folio No., Folio/Roll, Roll, Roll Number, Roll No., or Roll/Folio.
3. When the notice prints BOTH a Folio and a Roll number and the two differ, return the FOLIO value. The roll number is usually the same identifier with a jurisdiction prefix or a trailing sub-account added: folio '328-314-00-0' against roll 'D-328-314-00-0', folio '1987-9000-7' against roll '051-1987-9000-7', folio '23-0122-012' against roll '23-0122-012-000', folio '000592.002' against roll '0000592.002'. Only when no Folio label appears anywhere does the Roll number become the answer.
4. Prefer the value printed in the property details block. The remittance stub usually repeats the same number and sometimes abbreviates it; when the two differ, return the fuller form from the property details block.
5. Do not confuse the folio with the jurisdiction number printed beside it (a short three-digit municipality code such as 306 or 221), the PID or parcel identifier, the access code, the plan, lot or block number, the legal description, the customer or bulk owner code, a postal code, a date, or a dollar amount.
6. When the notice prints a distinct account number as well as a folio or roll number, return the folio or roll — the account number belongs to a different field. On most notices the two are the same number, and returning it is then correct.
7. Keep dashes, dots, letters and leading zeros exactly as printed, and remove only spaces printed between digit groups. Return null if no folio or roll number is printed.

bill_type.description: Classify by WHO issued the document/invoice/bill and what kind of biller they are — never by who is being billed. Municipal bill is issued by a government or municipal body — a city, town, regional district, or municipal utility — OR is an energy or water utility account statement (natural gas, electricity, water, sewer, stormwater), whether that utility is a government body or a private utility company. Includes energy and water/sewer/stormwater utility charges, business license and permit renewal fees, property tax, and other government or city-issued charges — including a garbage, waste, or recycling charge that appears on a government or city-issued utility bill. Return "municipal" for FortisBC natural gas bills, BC Hydro electricity bills, city water/sewer/stormwater bills, and similar energy or water utility account statements. Commercial document or invoice is issued by a private business — tradespeople and contractors (plumbing, electrical, HVAC, roofing, carpentry, restoration, general contracting, appliance repair, pest control), grounds and landscaping services, fire inspection service, private garbage, waste, and recycling collection or hauling companies (for example Waste Connections, GFL, Waste Management), private telecom, internet, and phone companies, insurers, and general suppliers. A private garbage/recycling/waste-hauling company that issues its own service invoice is commercial even though it handles waste; only a garbage or waste charge issued by a government or city body is municipal. If you cannot confirm the bill is a government or municipal charge or an energy or water utility account statement, output 'commercial'.

sub_bill_type.description: Classify the specific kind of bill by the primary charge being billed. Return 'gas' when the bill charges for natural gas service — natural gas usage in GJ (gigajoules), a gas meter reading, a 'natural gas' rate or delivery charge (for example a FortisBC natural gas bill). Return 'electric' when the bill charges for electricity service — electricity usage in kWh, an electricity meter reading, or electricity rate charges (for example a BC Hydro bill). A utility account statement is 'gas' or 'electric' based on the commodity actually charged on this bill, regardless of what else the utility company sells; if both commodities are charged, return the one with the larger charge. Return 'water' when a city or municipal utility bill charges for water, sewer, or stormwater service — including a combined city utility bill that also carries garbage, recycling, or other charge lines. Return 'propertytax' for a city or municipal property tax notice — an annual levy on a parcel of land, identified by a folio or roll number, assessed property values, and tax levy lines for general, school, or regional charges. A property tax notice is a municipal bill even when it is titled a notice rather than an invoice, and even when it carries a home owner grant claim or a tax sale warning. Return 'business_license' only for a city-issued bill whose charge is the licence to operate a business — a business licence or business permit renewal with a licence number, a business licence category or class (for example a trade or business type), and an annual business licence or renewal fee. A city-issued permit that regulates an activity or a property use is NOT a business licence: a towing permit notice, parking permit, sign permit, building or development permit, dog or animal licence, or any other bylaw permit renewal is 'other', even though it is city-issued, carries a permit or file number, and charges a renewal fee. Return 'repair' for an invoice issued by a private business — a tradesperson, contractor, or service company — for repair, maintenance, or service work that references the buyer's purchase order or job number. Return 'other' for everything else, including towing permit notices and other bylaw or activity permit renewals, other government or city charges, and any commercial invoice that is not for repair or service work or carries no purchase order or job number. Exactly one label applies to each document; when none of the specific definitions above is met, the answer is 'other'.

sub_bill_type_generate.description:
Determine the specific kind of bill this document is. Reason step by step:
1. Identify the biller and the primary charge being billed.
2. If the bill charges for natural gas service — natural gas usage in GJ (gigajoules), a gas meter reading, or a natural gas rate or delivery charge (for example a FortisBC natural gas bill) — the answer is gas.
3. If the bill charges for electricity service — usage in kWh, an electricity meter reading, or electricity rate charges (for example a BC Hydro bill) — the answer is electric. If both gas and electricity are charged, answer with the commodity carrying the larger charge.
4. If a city or municipal utility bill charges for water, sewer, or stormwater service — including a combined city utility bill that also carries garbage or recycling lines — the answer is water.
5. If the document is a city or municipal property tax notice — an annual levy on a parcel of land, with a folio or roll number, assessed values, and tax levy lines for general, school, or regional charges — the answer is propertytax. It is a property tax notice even when titled a notice rather than an invoice, and even when it carries a home owner grant claim or a tax sale warning.
6. If the document is a city-issued business licence renewal — the charge is the licence to operate a business, with a licence number, a business licence category or class, and an annual licence fee — the answer is business_license. A city permit that regulates an activity or a property use — a towing permit notice, parking permit, sign permit, building or development permit, dog or animal licence, or any other bylaw permit — is never business_license even though it is city-issued, has a permit or file number, and charges a renewal fee; for such a permit the answer is other.
7. If the document is an invoice issued by a private business — a tradesperson, contractor, or service company — for repair, maintenance, or service work and it references the buyer's purchase order or job number, the answer is repair.
8. Otherwise — including towing permit and other bylaw permit renewals, other government or city charges, and any commercial invoice that is not for repair or service work or carries no purchase order or job number — the answer is other.
Answer with exactly one of: gas, electric, water, propertytax, business_license, repair, other.

is_handwritten.description: Classify by how the field VALUES were produced, not by the form or letterhead. Classify yes when the value of any important field (vendor name, total amount, service address, GST amount, or PO/job number) is handwritten or manually filled in. A pre-printed blank invoice form — printed letterhead, printed field labels such as DATE/INVOICE/DESCRIPTION/PRICE, and a printed table grid — whose values (dates, amounts, totals, addresses, invoice or job numbers, descriptions) are written in by hand IS handwritten: classify yes even though the letterhead and labels are printed. Classify no only when those important field values themselves are printed or digitally generated; handwritten signatures, checkboxes, or margin notes on an otherwise fully printed invoice do not make it yes. This value is informational only.

is_handwritten_generate.description:
Determine whether this invoice's field values are handwritten. Reason step by step:
1. Decide what kind of document this is: a computer-generated invoice (uniform typeset fonts, perfectly aligned columns of numbers, a digitally laid out header, footer, and itemized table produced by software), or a paper form filled in by hand and then scanned or photographed.
2. A receipt book or carbon-copy sales pad page is the clearest handwritten case: a small pre-printed form with numbered row lines, boxes such as SOLD BY / C.O.D. / CHARGE / ON ACCT, a pre-printed serial number, and GST / PST / TOTAL boxes at the bottom, whose date, address, descriptions, and amounts were written in by hand — often with amounts in split dollars-and-cents columns with no decimal point. Such a page is handwritten even though its letterhead and printed labels are printed: the answer is yes.
3. More generally, look at the values of the important fields (the date, the address, the line-item descriptions and amounts, the GST and total amounts, and any invoice, PO, or job number). Handwritten values have irregular pen or pencil strokes, uneven character size, slant, and spacing, and sit unevenly on or across the printed lines; printed values are uniform typeset characters.
4. Recognition errors in the values are themselves evidence of handwriting: misread letters or digits (for example a street suffix read as 's7' instead of 'St'), stray or unreadable characters, or words that do not parse cleanly happen when text was written by hand, not when it was printed by software.
5. Ignore signatures, checkboxes, and margin notes: a fully printed invoice whose only hand marks are a signature, a checkbox, or a short note is not handwritten — the answer is no.
6. The answer is yes when the value of any important field is handwritten; the answer is no only when the important field values themselves are printed or digitally generated. A computer-generated invoice is unmistakable — uniform fonts and software layout throughout — so when the evidence is mixed or you are unsure, answer yes.
Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.

invoice_description.description: One very short phrase describing what this invoice is for, from the line items, Service For, or notes. Hard limit: under 44 characters including spaces and punctuation — about 4 to 6 short words. Name only the primary service; when the phrase would be too long, drop adjectives, brand or product names, and secondary services rather than exceed the limit: write 'Security monitoring service', never 'Intrusion security monitoring and GSM service'. Do not include vendor name, numbers, address, date, tax, or total. Do not mention GST. Examples: 'Lawn maintenance service in March.' 'Electrical repair work.' 'Monthly water utility charges in June.' 'Annual business license renewal for 2026.' Return an empty string if undeterminable.

diagnosis_solution.description:
Summarise what this vendor did — what they found and repaired, or what they supplied — for a property manager reading it months later. Reason step by step:
1. This applies only to a commercial vendor invoice. If the document is a municipal utility bill — water, sewer, electricity, natural gas, a business licence, or property tax — return an empty string.
2. Read the line-item descriptions and any Details of Repairs Performed, Description of Work, service note, or technician note.
3. Decide which kind of invoice this is: service work (an inspection, diagnosis, repair, or maintenance visit) or a supply of goods (an appliance, equipment, parts, or materials, usually with delivery or installation).
4. For service work, state the problem found and its cause where the invoice reports one — what was inspected, what was diagnosed, what was ruled out — and then the work performed. A finding of no fault is still a finding; report it.
5. For a supply of goods there is no diagnosis to report, and the summary is still required: describe what was supplied, delivered, installed, connected, or hauled away. Never answer with an empty string merely because no problem was diagnosed.
6. Write plain prose in the past tense, in ENGLISH. Other fields in this schema ask for Traditional Chinese; this one does not. Do not answer in Chinese.
7. Aim for 600 characters or fewer and never exceed 800; when it would run long, drop model numbers, part numbers, quantities, and repeated boilerplate rather than exceed the limit.
8. Do not include prices, tax, totals, the vendor name, the service address, or work that is only recommended rather than done.
Return an empty string only if the invoice describes neither work performed nor goods supplied.

recommendation.description:
Summarise work the vendor recommends doing in future but did NOT perform on this invoice. Reason step by step:
1. This applies only to a commercial vendor invoice. If the document is a municipal utility bill — water, sewer, electricity, natural gas, a business licence, or property tax — return an empty string.
2. Look for an Additional Work Recommended or Recommendations block, and for sentences anywhere in the line items or notes such as 'we recommend', 'strongly recommend', 'should be replaced', or 'needs attention'.
3. Report each recommended item, and the quoted amount for that future work where the invoice prints one.
4. Do not restate work that was already performed and billed on this invoice — that belongs elsewhere. A recommendation is something still to be done.
5. Write plain prose in ENGLISH. Other fields in this schema ask for Traditional Chinese; this one does not. Do not answer in Chinese.
6. Aim for 600 characters or fewer and never exceed 800; when it would run long, keep the recommended actions themselves and drop the reasoning behind them.
Return an empty string if the invoice recommends no further work.

warranty.description:
Summarise the warranty coverage printed on this invoice. Reason step by step:
1. This applies only to a commercial vendor invoice. If the document is a municipal utility bill — water, sewer, electricity, natural gas, a business licence, or property tax — return an empty string.
2. A value for this field must state a SPECIFIC warranty term: a length such as '1 year', '90 days' or 'lifetime', a covered period, or an expiration date. Look for a warranty or guarantee on the work or the goods, an extended warranty or service plan, or a manufacturer's warranty, and read the term, period, or dates printed with it.
3. If no specific term, period, or expiration date is printed anywhere, return an empty string — even when the document discusses warranties at length. Wording that names no term, such as 'certain products may have warranties provided by the manufacturer' or 'limited to service or repair by the manufacturer during the warranty period set out in the product warranty', is not a value for this field.
4. Report the coverage and its term ONLY. Do not report payment terms, late-payment interest, collection charges, or a returns and refunds policy, and do not report any disclaimer, limitation, exclusion, or denial — clauses such as 'repairs cannot be guaranteed', 'no other warranty is expressed or implied', 'the manufacturer and not the seller provides the warranty', or a list of what is not covered.
5. When one clause states both a term and a disclaimer, KEEP THE TERM AND DROP THE DISCLAIMER. From 'Appliances come with manufacturers warranty; no other warranty is expressed or implied. Includes a 1-year free warranty extension (January 17, 2026 - January 17, 2027)' return '1-year warranty extension, January 17, 2026 to January 17, 2027.' and nothing about what is excluded.
6. Write the summary in ENGLISH. Other fields in this schema ask for Traditional Chinese; this one does not. Do not answer in Chinese, and do not translate the invoice's wording into any other language.
7. Be brief: at most two short sentences stating the coverage and its term. Aim for 250 characters or fewer and never exceed 400.
Return an empty string when no specific warranty term, period, or expiration date is printed on the document.

diagnosis_solution_zh_hant.description:
Summarise what this vendor did — what they found and repaired, or what they supplied — written in Traditional Chinese. Reason step by step:
1. This applies only to a commercial vendor invoice. If the document is a municipal utility bill — water, sewer, electricity, natural gas, a business licence, or property tax — return an empty string.
2. Read the line-item descriptions and any Details of Repairs Performed, Description of Work, service note, or technician note.
3. Decide which kind of invoice this is: service work (an inspection, diagnosis, repair, or maintenance visit) or a supply of goods (an appliance, equipment, parts, or materials, usually with delivery or installation).
4. For service work, determine the problem found and its cause where the invoice reports one — including a finding that no fault was present — and then the work performed. For a supply of goods there is no diagnosis to report, and the summary is still required: describe what was supplied, delivered, installed, connected, or hauled away. Never answer with an empty string merely because no problem was diagnosed.
5. Write the summary in Traditional Chinese characters (繁體中文) as used in Hong Kong and Taiwan. Do not use Simplified Chinese characters. Do not answer in English.
6. Report the same facts, at the same level of detail, that a plain-language English summary of this invoice would report. Do not add model numbers, serial numbers, warranty terms, recycling or disposal fees, rebates, or verbatim line-item names that such a summary would leave out. Where you do mention a brand name or a date, keep it in the form printed on the invoice rather than translating or converting it.
7. Aim for 600 characters or fewer and never exceed 800. Do not include prices, tax, totals, the vendor name, the service address, or work that is only recommended rather than done.
Return an empty string only if the invoice describes neither work performed nor goods supplied.

anomaly_flag.description: Note genuine anomalies for a reviewer: vendor name missing, total amount missing, a total amount lower than the GST amount when GST is present, a GST amount that is clearly not about 5% of the pre-tax amount when GST is present, a suspiciously round total with no itemisation, or duplicate-looking line items. Do not flag a missing invoice number or a missing payment due date. Return an empty string if nothing is unusual.
